title: Button telemetry & animation-layer contracts for low-power mode
creator: Leah Kim
description: Problem: Several recent regressions surfaced where dense icon buttons and cancelable loading states animate in ways that increase CPU usage on low-power mobile devices and create inconsistent telemetry events across platforms. Goal: Define a clear design contract for the animation layer and telemetry signals emitted by button components so engineering can implement a low-power mode that (1) disables non-essential motion, (2) emits unified lifecycle telemetry (shown, start-loading, cancel, success, error), and (3) preserves accessibility semantics and visual clarity across themes and high-contrast modes. Scope: primary Button component + IconButton + SplitAction with loading states and cancel flows; theming token mappings for motion and reduced-motion; telemetry event naming and payload shape (minimal fields). Out of scope: global page-level perf instrumentation (handled by infra), complex motion prototypes for other components (separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design spec includes static token values and a motion flag that maps to component props (motion: full | reduced | none); 2) Figma variants for Button/IconButton showing stilled reduced-motion state and cancelable spinner states in all themes (light, dark, HC); 3) Telemetry schema documented: event names, required fields, and recommended sampling for high-frequency actions; 4) Dev has signoff from accessibility and runtime teams after a 1-week integration test; 5) No visual regressions in the button visual diff baseline across supported breakpoints.
